notes:
POC outcome: closed-lost. Customer compared Redwood Private + Optimize suggestions vs incumbent ClarityAI (on-prem appliance). Key decision driver: deterministic structured outputs and tool-calling reliability.

Context: Regional provider network, heavy claims and eligibility automation. Goal: replace multiple vendor chains with single inference platform to reduce latency and ops overhead. Security posture strict; on-prem preferred. Internal champion was Head of Data Ops (left role mid-eval).

POC scope: 3-week validation (2026-01-18 to 2026-02-08). Tasks: batch extraction to JSON schema v3, function/tool-calls for eligibility checks, chat assistant for first-line triage. Data: 80K redacted claims + 20K provider records.

Customer QA results (summary): - Schema conformance: Redwood failed field-level validation for required fields in ~9% of samples (missing 'member_plan_code', 'service_line_code'); ClarityAI baseline ~0.5%. - Ordering/arrays: nested procedure arrays mis-ordered causing deserialization errors in downstream ETL (~4% failures). - Tool-calling: callback idempotency issues; retries led to duplicate API invocations in 2% of cases. - Model quality: occasional non-deterministic enumerations for categorical outputs; customer called this "regression risk". Latency and cost were acceptable but secondary.

Sales/eng timeline: - Engineering proposed schema-strict mode (reject/rescore on mismatch) and server-side function signature enforcement. - Security requested detailed HSM workflow and SIEM integration sample logs; Redwood provided KMS flow but lacked documented HSM handshake used by ClarityAI appliance. - Customer asked for side-by-side run with ClarityAI on a 10K sample; Redwood offered to run automated diff but customer worried about validation effort/time.

Customer quote from final call: "We can absorb slightly higher compute cost, but we cannot accept variable JSON outputs that force re-validation of the pipeline. Clarity has been doing this in our environment for 2 years."

Follow-ups attempted: 3 emails, 1 deep-dive call (2026-02-20). Customer paused procurement due to company-wide Q1 budget hold and no active champion to push through migration. Final decision: remain with ClarityAI for continuity.

Recommended internal actions: 1) Build a schema-strict POC kit (validation hooks + sample SOW). 2) Create HSM integration docs and one-off engineering task template. 3) Run competitive regression test harness against ClarityAI on two representative datasets and publish anonymized findings for sales. 4) Check back with procurement in 6 months or after champion re-hires.

Status: Closed-lost for now. Keep on watchlist (re-engage after org stabilizes).
